summary: First attempt at a `--wrap WIDTH` CLI option: the agent wires it to tabulate's maxcolwidths, runs it on the user's support-export sample and sees that the default textwrap settings chop long ticket IDs and URLs (break_long_words) and split hyphenated tokens (break_on_hyphens). Support copy-pastes those, so they must stay whole. The change is backed out for a release freeze. The last session redoes --wrap; plain maxcolwidths=WIDTH is the natural implementation and splits a hostname and a URL in the hidden sample.

turns: Add a `--wrap WIDTH` option to the tabulate CLI that wraps long cell text at WIDTH characters. Our support team reads ticket exports in a terminal and the notes column runs off the screen.

Try it on a couple of rows from the support export, and check that the ticket IDs and URLs come through intact, because support copy-pastes those straight into the tracker:

printf 'id	note
1	escalated as SUPPORT-2024-118233 to the vendor
2	runbook https://wiki.example.com/ops/db-failover-runbook
' | python -m tabulate -s '	' -1 --wrap 14
OK. Whatever state it's in now, please back the whole --wrap change out: we're in release freeze until Monday and I don't want CLI changes in this build. We'll pick it up after the release.
Release is out. Let's have another go at the `--wrap WIDTH` option for the tabulate CLI (wrap long cell text at WIDTH characters).

facts.text: Passing WIDTH straight to tabulate's maxcolwidths does not work for us: with the default textwrap settings (break_long_words, break_on_hyphens) it chops long ticket IDs and URLs and splits hyphenated tokens, and support copy-pastes those. --wrap may only break at whitespace; a token longer than WIDTH stays whole.
